what: What the paper and the workshop decision asked for, against what this repository holds. `present` means the named material is here as files. It does not mean it is released, licensed, independently verified or runnable; those are stated per row.

sources_of_the_promises.paper: Availability paragraph of the version submitted for review: 'the mutation probes and their finding ledgers, the per-item adjudication records behind [the ledger table], the constraint-addition ledger with its per-commit machine sums, the predicate-audit ledger and per-predicate regression fixtures, the per-record rescore ledgers [...], and the preservation-annex records --- is retained internally and planned for an anonymized release with the benchmark artifact upon publication.'
sources_of_the_promises.decision: The acceptance decision: 'provide inspectable examples and the promised audit artifacts, identify executable scorer versions'.

promises.what_is_here: The two probe scripts as source: round 1 (false_success_probe.py) and round 2 (false_success_probe_full.py), each at the first commit that ran it and at the development pin. Two or three lines per file that named a local directory are rewritten to placeholders (provenance/TRANSFORMATIONS.json).
promises.what_is_missing: The probes cannot be run from this repository. They iterate over the 640 feasible scenarios of the corpus at the commit they ran on, and no corpus is held here. Only three probe findings can be replayed, as the worked cases.
promises.command: none for the probes; `python -m nlebench_audit cases` for the three worked cases

promises.promise: the finding ledgers of the probes
promises.what_is_here: Each tracked version of the two probe ledgers (four snapshots of round 1, three of round 2), with its dev-split findings, and the table of the 139 dev-split candidate sites reconciled from them with cause and disposition.
promises.what_is_missing: The findings and sites of the 600 test-split scenarios (388 of the 527 sites over both splits), and the 13 ledgers regenerated by re-running the probes in 2026-10. sites/recovery_168.csv is that run's accounting of the blocked keys whose block is recorded at site-key grain only, for the dev split (36 of 168): one row each, with the verdict pattern that was observed again. It does not say that those repairs were verified or those defects confirmed.
promises.command: `python -m nlebench_audit tables` recounts the site table

promises.promise: the per-item adjudication records behind the ledger table
promises.what_is_here: The triage, closeout and two hardening ledgers at the development pin, with their dev-split items, and the per-site table that carries their labels and the recorded reason for each disposition, for the dev split.
promises.what_is_missing: The items of the test-split scenarios. What does not exist: human validation or a second rater. The labels and reasons were generated in a coding-agent workflow. The notes are partly in Korean.

promises.promise: the constraint-addition ledger with its per-commit machine sums
promises.what_is_here: The 2026-08 ledger and the 2026-10 per-scenario history computed from git objects, with its dev-split examples; the history notes that the recorded ledger counts list lengths per commit.
promises.what_is_missing: The test-split examples of the history. The history cannot be recomputed here: it needs every scenario file at every commit.

promises.promise: the predicate-audit ledger and per-predicate regression fixtures
promises.what_is_here: The audit ledger, with its scenario lists reduced to the dev split; the 69 fixture cases, the meta-test and the fail-closed tests, runnable here on the pinned modules of the development pin.
promises.what_is_missing: The test-split scenario lists of the audit ledger; its counts cover both splits as recorded. The fixtures exercise the scorer of the development pin only. They say nothing about the snapshot scorer.

promises.what_is_here: The two 2026-08 ledgers (their rows reduced to the dev split, local directory names replaced at registered positions), and the 2026-10 tables for the dev split: one stored verdict per record and run for the 29,400 dev-split records, the signed differences of each comparison; the row table and the run stamps as recorded, over both splits.
promises.what_is_missing: The records of the test split (88,200 of the 117,600). The records themselves. `tables` re-counts stored verdicts; it does not judge a state and runs no agent. Judging the records again needs the raw run logs (about 1.7 GB) and the analysis code, which are not part of this repository.

promises.what_is_here: The 2026-08 record, byte-identical to the development pin.
promises.what_is_missing: It is not re-derived or re-checked by anything in this repository.

promises.what_is_here: Five worked cases. Three are deterministic probe findings with instruction, initial state, reference and candidate steps, both final states, the constraints before and after, and the verdict of every check. Two are stored agent runs of 2026-04 judged under the published and the current scorer.
promises.what_is_missing: For NLB-v3-CX-CO-002 and NLB-v3-EX-DE-008 four of the five analysed stages are held. The fifth (code before the repair with the new constraints) used a scenario assembled for that test, which is in no commit; its recorded verdicts are in case.json and cannot be replayed. Five cases are examples, not a sample.

promises.what_is_here: Three scorer files with repository, commit, path and file hash; the diffs of the modules that were swapped; and, for the five commits a replay needs, the surrounding modules as byte-identical git blobs.
promises.what_is_missing: A lock file: the benchmark tracks none at these commits, so dependency versions are the observed ones of one environment. A contract digest is not a hash of the code. The module sets are the import closure of the commands here, not the benchmark.

promises.promise: corpus fingerprints (identity of the three corpora compared)
promises.what_is_here: Both fingerprint definitions and the expected hashes for the published corpus, the v3.1 corpus of the submission and the v3.2 corpus of the development pin.
promises.what_is_missing: The corpora. `fingerprint` recomputes a hash only when given a scenario directory; none is held here.
The raw logs, the analysis code and the full source trees. This is by design and is not a gate of this repository.

promises.promise: independent verification of any label or number
promises.what_is_here: Nothing. The labels were generated in a coding-agent workflow, and the runs were made on a Someple Inc. server through a coding agent.
promises.what_is_missing: A second rater, a rerun by someone else, a rerun of any agent.
